### [location] Org invite validation: server vs client enforcement map  (id: org-invite-validation-server-vs-client-enforcement-map, confidence 85%)
Server (posthog/api/organization_invite.py):
- `OrganizationInviteSerializer.validate_target_email`: EmailNormalizer.normalize, `reject_plus_addressed_email`, `validate_invite_target_email_domain` (also used in `OrganizationInviteViewSet.delegate`).
- `validate_first_name` -> `validate_display_name`; `validate_message` -> `validate_message_body` (posthog/helpers/email_utils.py).
- `validate_level` raises PermissionDenied if level > inviter's; `validate_private_project_access` checks project access levels (member/admin only); model re-checks JSON shape in posthog/models/organization_invite.py.
- `create` rejects invitee who is already a member (case-insensitive on user__email).
- Permissions: `UserCanInvitePermission` (posthog/permissions.py) + TimeSensitiveActionPermission; throttles Burst 50/h, Sustained 200/d in `get_throttles`; max 20 per `bulk`.
- Accept: `OrganizationInvite.validate`/`use` (expiry INVITE_DAYS_VALIDITY=3 days, email, membership).
Client: `isEmail` in InviteRow, `canSubmit` + `inviteContainsOwnerLevel` (owner confirmation is client-only) in inviteLogic.ts, `MAX_INVITES_AT_ONCE` in InviteModal.tsx, allowedLevels filtered <= membership_level. Plus, domain, name/message content and project checks are server-only; errors surface only from the response.
→ pointers: posthog/api/organization_invite.py:OrganizationInviteSerializer:L166, posthog/permissions.py:UserCanInvitePermission:L1360, posthog/api/organization_invite.py:OrganizationInviteSerializer.validate_target_email:L196, posthog/helpers/email_utils.py:EmailNormalizer.normalize:L247, posthog/api/organization_invite.py:OrganizationInviteViewSet.delegate:L534, posthog/models/organization_invite.py:OrganizationInvite.validate:L103 (+4 more)
